chapter: Teddy Wilson bands and Cafe Society
title: The dedicated Teddy Wilson band outplays Benny Goodman's
summary: Hall describes discipline, the sidemen, and the night Goodman left his own band to play with Wilson's rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: What else do you remember about Teddy's band besides the fact that it was very sophisticated?

It was a most decidated band. Dedicated bunch of guys that I had ever been with during our short span. when we played at the Golden Guts Ballroom Nobody was ever late. If we had rehearsal, the reeds would rehearse in one section, maybe the ladies room, and the brass would rehearse in the men's room and we'd come on the
bandstand and everybody had to get an 'A' (inaudible) and our rhythm section was a gas. Buster Harding, Buster Harding was the arranger, but we had two pianists. He played with Teddy.
Right. And Ben Webster was in that band?

Yeah. Ben Webster, George (inaudible), Rudy Powell, Pete Clark and everybody got the same mouthpiece, the same sound style. We played against Benny Goodman on a union gig, a union benefit there and we were on one side of the bandstand and Benny's got his band on the other side of the bandstand. We wiped out that band. Benny left his band and came over to us. J.C. and Teddy and me, he played with us and he left the band there and they hadn't played a note. (Laughter)
Benny was so grooved with your band that, with Teddy's band, that he came over and played with the whole big band or just the rhythm section?
And left his band sitting there?
They must have been pretty hacked at that?
